passage:
The school app sent homework notices, grades, lunch menus, and activity updates. It was useful, but notifications arrived all day.
Students and parents began ignoring them because there were too many.
The school changed the system. Urgent messages came immediately. Normal updates were sent once in the evening.
People read the messages more carefully after that.
The app taught the school that communication is not improved by simply sending more information. Too many messages can become noise.
Attention is limited. Good communication respects that limit by sorting what matters now from what can wait.
